arguments.summary: Completed-session evidence supports a conditional 63-session technical preference for NVDA over MU, not an all-window preference. NVDA had stronger 63-session absolute and benchmark-relative returns, a shallower 63-session close-path drawdown, and a close above its prior 21-session closing high. MU had positive 21- and 63-session momentum but negative five-session returns and excess returns, remained below its prior 21-session closing high, and showed materially greater path risk. The market was closed; dated completed SIP closes, not stale single-venue IEX observations, anchor the analysis.

claims.text: NVDA's 2026-10-02 split-adjusted SIP close was $233.95. Completed-session price returns were +3.9454% over 5 sessions, +4.2511% over 21, and +19.6369% over 63. The close was 4.54% above SMA20 ($223.786), 7.18% above SMA50, and 16.56% above SMA200. SMA20 rose 0.9161% over five sessions; the close was 1.3385% above the prior 21-session closing high. Last-session volume was 1.3382x the prior-20-session median and recent-five-session average volume was 1.1189x. The observed 63-session maximum close-path drawdown was -10.5835%. Annualized realized volatility was 14.8821%, 24.8521%, and 38.2473% over 5/21/63 sessions; these are historical path measures, not forecasts.

Matched 2026-10-02 split-adjusted SIP price-return comparisons: PAIR NVDA/SPY 5=+4.1671 21=+3.6656 63=+17.1931. PAIR NVDA/XLK 5=+2.1418 21=-4.5778 63=+10.7902. NVDA/SPY excess was positive at 5, 21, and 63 sessions. NVDA/XLK excess was positive at 5 and 63 sessions but negative at 21 sessions; therefore the recent absolute rise and 63-session sector-relative strength coexist with 21-session sector-relative weakness.

NVDA's strongest continuation evidence for the 63-session mandate is its +19.6369% absolute return, +17.1931-point excess versus SPY, +10.7902-point excess versus XLK, close above the prior 21-session closing high, and rising SMA20. Its strongest opposing path is short-term extension—RSI14 was 82.97—combined with the negative 21-session excess versus XLK. Thus trend in NVDA's price level is favorable, but sector leadership is window-dependent rather than uniform.

For NVDA's coarse current regime—close above SMA20, SMA20 above SMA50, and positive 21-session return—the overlapping historical sample numbered 265. Positive forward-return frequencies were 58.1132%, 58.4906%, and 71.6981% over 5/21/63 sessions versus unconditional base rates of 58.8697%, 61.6954%, and 73.4694% from 637 observations. The regime frequencies were lower than the respective base rates at each horizon. The conditional 63-session p10/p90 range was -8.4506% to +40.1616%. These dependent finite-lookback observations are neither calibrated probabilities nor causal evidence.

The market was closed. NVDA's completed SIP close of $233.95 on 2026-10-02 is the analytical price anchor. The latest IEX trade was $234 at 19:59:59.998859 UTC that day, but no IEX quote was available; this single-venue trade is not a current consolidated executable quote.

MU's 2026-10-02 split-adjusted SIP close was $1,074.89. Completed-session price returns were -0.6828% over 5 sessions, +12.4268% over 21, and +9.1536% over 63. The close was 4.87% above SMA20 ($1,025.0015), 12.43% above SMA50, and 57.70% above SMA200. SMA20 rose 3.1041% over five sessions, but the close remained 2.0503% below the prior 21-session closing high. Last-session volume was 1.1404x the prior-20-session median and recent-five-session average volume was 1.2522x. The observed 63-session maximum close-path drawdown was -25.4770%. Annualized realized volatility was 36.5718%, 49.5463%, and 74.5624% over 5/21/63 sessions.

Matched 2026-10-02 split-adjusted SIP price-return comparisons: PAIR MU/SPY 5=-0.4611 21=+11.8413 63=+6.7098. PAIR MU/XLK 5=-2.4865 21=+3.5978 63=+0.3068. MU's excess return was negative versus both comparators at 5 sessions and positive versus both at 21 and 63 sessions. The 63-session XLK excess was positive but narrow at +0.3068 percentage points, so medium- and mandate-window leadership coexisted with recent lag.

MU's continuation case rests on a sharply rising SMA20, positive 21/63-session absolute returns, and positive 21/63-session excess returns versus SPY and XLK. The opposing path is substantial: its negative five-session return and excess returns, failure to regain the prior 21-session closing high, 74.5624% annualized 63-session realized volatility, and -25.4770% 63-session close-path drawdown show that positive endpoint returns masked considerable path risk. One volume ratio does not establish persistent breakout participation.

For MU's coarse current regime—close above SMA20, SMA20 above SMA50, and positive 21-session return—the overlapping historical sample numbered 306. Positive forward-return frequencies were 59.1503%, 67.6471%, and 79.0850% over 5/21/63 sessions versus unconditional base rates of 57.9278%, 63.4223%, and 71.1146% from 637 observations. Conditional frequencies exceeded base rates in this finite sample, but the conditional 63-session p10/p90 range was -15.9730% to +81.1562%. Dependence, regime selection, and wide outcomes preclude treating these as calibrated probabilities or guarantees.

The market was closed. MU's completed SIP close of $1,074.89 on 2026-10-02 is the analytical price anchor. The latest IEX trade was $1,074.71 at 19:59:58.451494 UTC; the IEX bid/ask just after 20:00 UTC was $1,030.27/$1,141.62. These stale single-venue observations do not establish a current consolidated executable quote.

For the 63-session window specifically, NVDA had the stronger completed-session technical record: absolute return was +19.6369% versus MU's +9.1536%; excess versus SPY was +17.1931 points versus +6.7098; excess versus XLK was +10.7902 versus +0.3068; and maximum close-path drawdown was -10.5835% versus -25.4770%. This is a 63-session market-behavior comparison only. It does not extend to every window: at 21 sessions MU had the stronger sector-relative result, +3.5978 points versus NVDA's -4.5778 points against XLK.

gaps.description: The forward-return panels use overlapping observations from one finite 2023-12-18 to 2026-07-06 lookback and a coarse three-sign regime. Non-overlapping, out-of-sample, and alternative-regime tests would be needed for stronger empirical conviction; this limits probability interpretation but does not block dated descriptive conclusions.

One last-session and one recent-five-session volume ratio cannot establish sustained participation. Subsequent completed closes with recomputed volume, prior-high distance, and matched benchmark excess returns are needed to test persistence.

assumptions: Comparisons use matched 2026-10-02 completed sessions, SIP feed, split-adjusted prices, and price returns; dividends are excluded.
Moving-average thresholds are frozen 2026-10-02 observations, not future dynamic averages or trading instructions.
Annualized realized volatility is the sample standard deviation of completed daily close-to-close returns times the square root of 252; it is not a forecast.
The relative technical preference applies only to the 63-session window and excludes valuation, earnings, policy, and fundamental judgments.
arguments.counter_thesis: NVDA's high RSI and negative 21-session excess versus XLK could precede consolidation despite positive five- and 63-session sector-relative results. MU could reaccelerate because its 21-session benchmark excess and rising SMA20 remain favorable, but its negative five-session excess, narrow +0.3068-point 63-session XLK edge, and deeper drawdown make that path less confirmed. No broad cross-asset causal confirmation was established here, so these remain stock-specific conditional setups.

review_conditions.description: An NVDA completed split-adjusted SIP close below the frozen 2026-10-02 SMA20 of $223.786 before expiry would weaken the near-term price trend and prompt reassessment, though it would not alone prove loss of 63-session relative strength.

For NVDA, recompute matched SIP split-adjusted excess returns after subsequent completed sessions. Positive 21- and 63-session excess versus both SPY and XLK would broaden the currently mixed sector-relative setup; negative 63-session excess versus both would invalidate the present 63-session technical preference.

A MU completed split-adjusted SIP close below the frozen 2026-10-02 SMA20 of $1,025.0015 before expiry would weaken the rising-trend setup and raise the relevance of its observed high-volatility drawdown path.

For MU, recompute matched SIP split-adjusted excess returns after subsequent completed sessions. Positive five-session excess versus both SPY and XLK while 21/63-session excess stays positive would confirm renewed short-window leadership; negative 21- or 63-session excess versus both would materially weaken continuation.

agent_report.work_summary: Analyzed supplied completed-session return, moving-average, volume, drawdown, realized-volatility, exact benchmark-comparison, IEX snapshot, and historical regime panels for NVDA and MU. Cross-checked each 5/21/63-session direction separately and distinguished completed SIP closes from stale single-venue snapshot observations.
main_conclusions: NVDA had the stronger 63-session technical record, with larger absolute and relative gains, a close above its prior 21-session closing high, and a shallower drawdown.
NVDA's leadership was not uniform: its 21-session excess versus XLK was negative despite positive 5- and 63-session XLK excess.

MU retained positive 21/63-session momentum and relative returns but had negative five-session performance, remained below its prior 21-session high, and showed materially greater volatility and drawdown.
Historical regime frequencies are descriptive finite-sample observations, not calibrated probabilities; NVDA's conditional positive-return frequencies were below base rates, while MU's were above.
Completed 2026-10-02 SIP closes anchor the analysis; IEX snapshots do not provide current consolidated executable quotes.
agent_report.short_summary: For the 63-session window only, NVDA is the cleaner conditional technical setup and MU is the higher-path-risk setup. Window-specific relative performance remains mixed, so continuation requires recomputed leadership confirmation rather than extrapolation from one horizon.
limitations: No causal attribution from returns or volume was made.
No valuation, earnings, policy, or fundamental conclusion is included.
Historical forward-return frequencies were not independently tested out of sample and use overlapping observations.
The routed cross-asset confirmation question remained unresolved.
